key_insight: The paper shows that two-qubit concurrence and three-qubit 3-tangle can be measured directly by quantum circuits using ancilla-assisted unitary transformations and output probabilities.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to characterize entanglement on hardware without full state tomography, reducing measurement overhead for quantum communication and quantum computing experiments.
method: Add auxiliary qubits to the target quantum state.
Use specific controlled unitary operations to encode entanglement formulas into measurable probabilities.
Read out ancilla/output measurement probabilities to extract concurrence or 3-tangle directly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the proposed circuit schemes directly map analytical entanglement expressions to measurement probabilities, enabling quantitative measurement without full quantum state tomography.
watch_item: The approach is presented for pure two-qubit and three-qubit states, so extension to noisy, mixed, or larger-scale hardware settings may require additional calibration and validation.
paper_title: Entanglement Detection for Two-Qubit and Three-Qubit Pure States via Unitary Transformations and Ancilla State Measurements
